title: Closer to Conductor, distinctly Sylph
question: All three keep the nested Repository → Workspace rail and familiar IDE density. Choose where Sylph should depart from Conductor.

options.label: Browser-First Sylph
options.thesis: Keep the proven IDE shell, but make the running product—not the transcript—the center of gravity.
options.viewport: A nested Repository and Workspace rail stays left; the live browser dominates the center; the agent thread stays visible at right; Changes, Checks, Console, and Skills share a precise lower evidence deck.
options.risk: Browser dominance must still leave enough continuous space for long agent conversations and code review.

options.label: Thread-First Sylph
options.lineage: Conductor conversation flow, Sylph live preview
options.thesis: Preserve the agent narrative as the main surface while making browser proof persistent instead of tab-bound.
options.viewport: The nested Repository and Workspace rail stays left; the agent thread and composer own the center; a tall live browser sits above Changes and Checks on the right; browser-control state remains visible globally.
options.risk: It is closest to Conductor and could feel derivative unless the preview behavior and Sylph color system carry real authority.

options.label: Adaptive Split
options.lineage: dense tiling IDEs with task-aware pane ratios
options.thesis: One stable shell changes its center of gravity as the user moves from prompting to watching to reviewing.
options.viewport: The nested Repository and Workspace rail stays left; agent and browser share the center in a deliberate 40/60 split; the right inspector holds Files, Changes, Checks, and Skills; one-key focus modes expand either center surface.
options.risk: Adaptive ratios become disorienting if the transition is not predictable and reversible.

canonCard.label: Conductor-adjacent baseline
canonCard.thesis: A polished dense dark IDE that groups repositories and Workspaces at left, keeps agent work central, and places changes and terminal tools at right.
canonCard.viewport: A direct familiar three-pane shell sits alongside Conductor, bb, and Diffs with minimal structural departure.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately usable and gives Sylph almost no visual territory of its own.
